quote: But I maintain that she would come if we worked for her, and that so to work, even in poverty and obscurity, is worth while.
source: Virginia Woolf, A Room of One’s Own, chapter 6, the closing sentence (1929)

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg Australia full text of A Room of One’s Own, fetched and the last paragraph read in place; the sentence is the final one before THE END
evidence.edition: A Room of One’s Own (Hogarth Press, 1929); Gutenberg Australia 0200791h
evidence.locator: Chapter 6, last sentence of the book, after “that we cannot expect, for that would be impossible.”

reason: The sentence is the last of the book, word for word and comma for comma as proposed, with “worth while” as two words. It is Woolf’s own voice, not a character’s. Not shipped, Woolf unused this year, not banned.
